//: Cannon clone-source lockfile for the devnet omnibus (PRO-998).
Every ref below is a `clone.*` source in packages/tomls/src/devnet/**, declared as a
*Package setting in src/omnibus/reya_devnet.toml. Cannon resolves a clone source through
the on-chain registry, and for these refs the registry now serves DIFFERENT artifact bytes
than devnet was actually deployed from (they were rebuilt on a newer cannon toolchain and
republished). Cannon clones proxies via CREATE2, so different artifact bytes mean different
initcode, a different proxy address, and a devnet that only reproduces on the one machine
whose local cache still holds the original artifacts.
`deploy` is the package's deployment blob -- the CID devnet was actually built from.
`misc` is the artifact blob that deployment blob points at (its `miscUrl`); the clone step
reads it unconditionally for contract bytecode, so a pin is only usable if BOTH are
reachable. Both are pinned here because both are inputs to the CREATE2 address.
chainId 13370 is not a typo: cannon resolves `clone.source` at CANNON_CHAIN_ID (the
portable/cross-chain variant), never at the target chain -- see @usecannon/builder
steps/clone.js, `config.chainId ?? CANNON_CHAIN_ID`. Priming these under 89346162 writes
tags no clone step ever reads.
Prime with `yarn reya_devnet:prime` BEFORE any devnet build. Cannon consults the local
registry before the on-chain ones, so priming makes every machine resolve these bytes.
The other five devnet clone sources (core/passivePerp/ordersGateway/periphery 1.1.2@router
and passive-pool 1.0.14@router) are NOT pinned: the registry still serves the artifacts
devnet was built from for those, so there is nothing to correct.
Verify a pin end-to-end with packages/tomls/scripts/verify-clone-source-pins.js, which
recomputes the devnet PassivePool CREATE2 address from these bytes.
